hints: Every weak component of a functional graph contains exactly one directed cycle, with trees feeding into it.
Rooted labelled trees have exponential generating function T satisfying T = z exp(T).
Use Lagrange inversion and unsigned Stirling numbers to calculate all component counts in quadratic time.
analogy: Each component is a cycle of trees: the cycle connects the trees while every other edge points toward it.
example: For n=3 there are 17 functional graphs with one component, 9 with two, and 1 with three.
algorithm: Let c(j,k) be the unsigned Stirling number of the first kind, with c(0,0)=1 and c(j,k)=c(j-1,k-1)+(j-1)c(j-1,k). Precompute factorials and inverse factorials modulo 10^9+7. For each k=1..n compute (n-1)! times the sum over j=k-1..n-1 of c(j+1,k) * n^(n-1-j) / ((n-1-j)! j!). Print each sum modulo the prime.
correctness: The generating function marking components by u is (1-T)^(-u). Lagrange inversion gives n![z^n](1-T)^(-u) = (n-1)! [t^(n-1)] u(1-t)^(-u-1)exp(nt). Expanding the rising factorial u(u+1)...(u+j) using c(j+1,k) yields exactly the stated coefficient.
complexity: O(n^2) time and O(n^2) space for the Stirling table; powers and factorials take O(n) extra space.
